questions.question: If the surface area of a sphere is 2124(4)/(7) cm², then what is the radius of that sphere? [Use π = (22)/(7)]

Surface Area (S) = 2124⁴⁄₇ cm²

S = 4πr²

Where, r = radius

⇒ r² = (2124⁴⁄₇ × 7) ÷ (4 × 22)

⇒ r² = 14871 ÷ 88

⇒ r² = 169

⇒ r = √169

⇒ r = 13 cm

questions.question: The present age of a father is 1(1)/(2) times the sum of the present ages of his two sons. Six years hence, the ratio of his age to the sum of the ages of his sons will be 6 ∶ 5. The present age of the father is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Father's present age = 1(1/2) times the sum of the present ages of his two sons.

Six years hence, the ratio of father's age to the sum of the ages of his sons = 6 ∶ 5.

**Formula used:**

Let the sum of the present ages of the two sons be x years.

Father's present age = 1.5x years

In 6 years, father's age = 1.5x + 6

In 6 years, sum of the ages of the two sons = x + 12

According to the given ratio:

((1.5x + 6))/((x + 12)) = (6)/(5)

**Calculation:**

((1.5x + 6))/((x + 12)) = (6)/(5)

⇒ 5(1.5x + 6) = 6(x + 12)

⇒ 7.5x + 30 = 6x + 72

⇒ 7.5x - 6x = 72 - 30

⇒ 1.5x = 42

⇒ x = 28

Father's present age = 1.5x = 1.5 × 28 = 42 years

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: A dishonest shopkeeper pretends to sell his goods at cost price, but uses a false weight on which 984 gm is written but which actually weighs much less. Using this false weight the shopkeeper actually makes a gain of 23%. Find the actual measure of the weight used.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A dishonest shopkeeper pretends to sell his goods at cost price but uses a false weight on which 984 gm is written but which actually weighs much less.

Using this false weight the shopkeeper actually makes a gain of 23%.

**Formula used:**

Let the actual weight be x gm.

Gain% = (False Weight - Actual Weight)/(Actual Weight) times 100

**Calculation:**

Gain% = 23%

⇒ 23 = (984 - x)/(x) times 100

⇒ 0.23 = (984 - x)/(x) 

⇒ 0.23x = 984 - x

⇒ 0.23x + x = 984

⇒ 1.23x = 984

⇒ x = (984)/(1.23) 

⇒ x = 800 gm

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: Which is the most commonly used measure for the size of the economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gross domestic product (GDP)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gross domestic product (GDP)** is the most commonly used measure for the size of the economy.
 
• GDP represents the total monetary value of all finished goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific time period, typically annually or quarterly.
 
• It includes all private and public consumption, government outlays, investments, and exports minus imports that occur within a defined territory.
 
• GDP is a comprehensive measure of a nation's overall economic activity and is often used to gauge the health of an economy.
 
• Higher GDP values typically indicate a prosperous economy, while lower GDP values may indicate economic struggles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross National Product (GNP)** is another measure of economic activity, but it includes the value of all goods and services produced by a country's residents, regardless of the location of production.
 
• **Net Domestic Product (NDP)** is derived from GDP by subtracting depreciation on a country’s capital goods.
 
• **Net National Product (NNP)** is GNP minus depreciation.
 
• The **GDP growth rate** is an important indicator of economic performance, showing how fast an economy is growing or shrinking over time.
 
• GDP can be measured using three approaches: the production (or output) approach, the income approach, and the expenditure approach.
 
• GDP per capita is often used as an indicator of the standard of living in a country, dividing the GDP by the population size.

questions.question: Which option is correct regarding the movement of water and mineral ions in the root cells of a plant from the soil?

Water moves in first by diffusion, followed by active transport of ions

questions.question: The radius of curvature of a concave mirror is 12 cm. Following New Cartesian Sign Convention, the principal focus is located at x = __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-6 cm**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The radius of curvature (R) of a concave mirror is given as 12 cm.
 
• According to the New Cartesian Sign Convention, the radius of curvature for a concave mirror is taken as negative.
 
• The relationship between the focal length (f) and the radius of curvature (R) of a concave mirror is given by the formula: f=(R)/(2)
 
• Substituting the given value: f=(-12)/(2)=-6cm
 
• Hence, the principal focus is located at x = -6 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the New Cartesian Sign Convention, distances measured against the direction of the incident light are taken as negative, while those measured along the direction of the incident light are taken as positive.
 
• For concave mirrors, the focal point and the center of curvature lie on the same side as the reflecting surface, hence their distances are considered negative.
 
• This sign convention helps in deriving and applying the mirror formula and magnification formula correctly.

questions.question: Two train engines of same length are running in the same direction with speeds of 18 km/h and 36 km/h. If the faster engine crosses the slower one in 8 sec, what is the length of each train engine?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of slower engine (S₁) = 18 km/h

Speed of faster engine (S₂) = 36 km/h

Time (t) = 8 sec

**Formula used:**

Relative Speed = S₂ - S₁

Distance = Relative Speed × Time

Length of each train engine = Distance / 2

**Calculation:**

Relative Speed = 36 km/h - 18 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed = 18 km/h

Convert Relative Speed to m/s: 18 km/h = 18 × (1000/3600) m/s

⇒ Relative Speed = 5 m/s

Distance = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ Distance = 5 m/s × 8 s

⇒ Distance = 40 m

Length of each train engine = Distance / 2

⇒ Length of each train engine = 40 m / 2

⇒ Length of each train engine = 20 m

questions.question: The numerator of a fraction is one less than the denominator. If 6 is added to the numerator, the fraction will be equal to (5)/(4). Find the fraction.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The numerator is 1 less than the denominator.

If 6 is added to the numerator, the fraction becomes 5/4.

**Formula used:**

Let the denominator be x, then the numerator is x - 1.

When 6 is added to the numerator:

(x - 1 + 6)/x = 5/4

**Calculation:**

⇒ (x + 5)/x = 5/4

⇒ 4(x + 5) = 5x

⇒ 4x + 20 = 5x

⇒ 20 = 5x - 4x

⇒ x = 20

⇒ Numerator = x - 1 = 20 - 1 = 19

**∴ The fraction is 19/20.**

questions.question: A chemical that contributes to the depletion of the ozone layer is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**chlorofluorocarbon**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)** are the primary chemical compounds that contribute to the depletion of the ozone layer.
 
• CFCs are used in various applications such as **refrigerants, propellants in aerosol sprays, and solvents** in the manufacturing industry.
 
• When CFCs are released into the atmosphere, they eventually reach the stratosphere where they are broken down by ultraviolet radiation, releasing chlorine atoms.
 
• **Chlorine atoms** react with ozone (O₃) molecules, causing the ozone molecules to break apart into oxygen molecules (O₂), thus depleting the ozone layer.
 
• The depletion of the ozone layer increases the amount of harmful **ultraviolet (UV) radiation** reaching the Earth's surface, which can lead to adverse environmental and health effects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Montreal Protocol**, adopted in 1987, is an international treaty designed to phase out the production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances, including CFCs.
 
• Since the implementation of the Montreal Protocol, there has been a significant reduction in the emission of CFCs, and the ozone layer is showing signs of recovery.
 
• Other chemicals that contribute to ozone depletion include **halons, carbon tetrachloride, and methyl chloroform**, but CFCs are the most well-known and widely used.
 
• It is crucial to continue monitoring and regulating these substances to ensure the continued recovery and protection of the ozone layer.

• While transpiration has several advantages, such as providing water for photosynthesis, transporting mineral ions, and cooling the plant through evaporation, it can also lead to wilting if the water loss exceeds the water uptake.

• It also helps in maintaining the temperature of the plant by cooling it through the evaporation process.
 
• However, excessive transpiration can lead to water stress, especially in arid conditions or during periods of drought.
 
• Plants have evolved various mechanisms to minimize water loss, such as closing their stomata, developing thick cuticles, and having reduced leaf surface area.

• As the ITCZ moves southwards, the southwest monsoon winds weaken, and the northeast monsoon winds begin to dominate.
 
• These winds pick up moisture from the Bay of Bengal and bring rainfall to the southeastern coast of India.
 
• The northeast monsoon is relatively less intense compared to the southwest monsoon but is vital for the water resources in Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: The refractive indices of ice and glass are 1.31 and 1.52, respectively. A ray of light passes from ice to glass. The refractive index of glass with respect to ice is __________ and the ray bends _________ the normal in glass.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4: 1.16, towards**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **refractive index of glass with respect to ice** is calculated by dividing the refractive index of glass by that of ice, which gives a value of **1.16**.
 
• As given in the question, the ray of light passes from ice to glass, and **the refractive index of ice is less than that of glass**.
 
• When light passes from a medium of lower refractive index to a higher refractive index, the ray bends **towards the normal**.
 
• In this case, since the refractive index of glass is higher than that of ice, the ray bends **towards the normal in glass**.
 
• This bending of light is governed by Snell’s law, which relates the angle of incidence and refraction to the refractive indices of the two media.

• **Refractive Index:** The refractive index (n) of a material is the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to the speed of light in the material. It indicates how much light is bent or refracted when entering the material from another medium.

• **Light Behavior:** When light moves from a less dense medium to a denser one (lower to higher refractive index), it bends towards the normal. Conversely, it bends away from the normal when it moves from a denser to a less dense medium.
